This proposal is regarding Post Breach Scenario Testing and providing clarity/visibility to XYZ LLC on whether the implemented defenses, particularly antivirus and endpoint protection controls, are working as expected or if there are hidden gaps that allow attacker-style antivirus bypass techniques within the environment.

Conduct a controlled, non-destructive Post Breach Scenario – Antivirus Bypass Assessment simulating realistic attacker techniques against XYZ LLC’s antivirus / endpoint defenses within agreed environments.

Evaluate the effectiveness of antivirus / EDR / endpoint security controls in detecting and blocking malicious commands, scripts and payloads with malware-like properties across on-disk and in-memory vectors.
Provide clear technical and executive-level reporting on antivirus bypass feasibility, detection gaps and recommended hardening actions to improve post breach resilience.
Post breach style Antivirus Bypass Analysis focused on assessing how attacker techniques can evade existing antivirus / EDR solutions within the agreed XYZ LLC environment.
Analysis of antivirus and endpoint configurations for detecting and blocking on-disk payloads, scripts and fileless in-memory execution patterns.
Execution of controlled, non-destructive antivirus bypass techniques aligned to real-world attacker tradecraft, with continuous coordination with XYZ LLC stakeholders.
Documentation of gaps where malicious behaviour is not detected, partially detected or incorrectly handled by current defenses.
NIST SP 800-115 – Technical Guide to Information Security Testing & Assessment (adapted for antivirus / endpoint testing).

MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise Matrix – focus on T1055 (Process Injection), T1055.012 (Process Hollowing), T1055.001 (DLL Injection), T1027 (Obfuscated/Encrypted Files or Information), T1055.004 (DLL Side-Loading) and related TTPs.
OSSTMM – relevant sections for system and endpoint evaluation under controlled conditions.
CIS Benchmarks and vendor baselines for endpoint / antivirus / EDR configurations (where applicable).
CERT-In Cyber Security Framework & advisories (for reference of regional best practices where applicable).

The Post Breach Antivirus Bypass Assessment focuses specifically on analysing whether a realistic attacker, having already gained an initial foothold, can bypass XYZ LLC’s antivirus and endpoint security solutions through on-disk and in-memory techniques. The objective is to determine how effectively the current defenses detect, block and log malicious behaviour without causing any destructive impact on the environment.
Review of current antivirus / EDR architecture, policies, update mechanisms and integration with central logging / SIEM.
Obfuscation of payloads, scripts and binaries to test signature and heuristic detection.
Packing techniques to compress and transform executables while maintaining functionality.
Use of Protectors to hinder reverse engineering and debugging, and to observe AV/EDR reaction.
Cryptor-based encryption/wrapping of payloads with in-memory decryption to test AV detection of unpacked code.
In-memory Antivirus Bypass Testing including controlled use of:
Memory Process Injection using Windows APIs such as OpenProcess(), VirtualAllocEx(), WriteProcessMemory(), GetModuleHandle(), GetProcAddress(), CreateRemoteThread() (where approved and safe).
Hooking techniques to alter execution flow and trigger hidden malicious logic while normal functions continue.
Process Hollowing - replacing the memory image of a suspended legitimate process with controlled test payloads and observing detection.
DLL Injection (on disk and in memory) to evaluate how DLL-based execution is handled by AV/EDR.
Analysis of antivirus reaction across all tested techniques including alerts, blocking, quarantine, process termination and logging behaviour.
Identification of bypass scenarios where malicious behaviour is executed without adequate detection, blocking or logging.
Correlation of antivirus bypass opportunities with potential post breach attack paths (e.g., lateral movement, privilege escalation, data access) for prioritised remediation.

The Active Directory Security Assessment is a

of the AD environment. It focuses on how design decisions, misconfigurations, and legacy controls can be abused by an attacker to escalate privileges from normal user to domain admin, persist in the environment, and compromise critical business systems. This process involves a thorough analysis of:
- Forests, domains, trusts, and administrative boundaries.
- Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Schema Admins, custom privileged groups.
- Hardening of domain controllers, member servers, and workstations through Group Policy.
- Delegation, ticket lifetimes, encryption types, SPNs, and service accounts.
- Template misconfigurations and certificate abuse possibilities.
- Excessive permissions on objects, containers, and admin groups.
- Password policies, lockout policies, stale accounts, and privileged service accounts.
- Events, audit policies, and integration with SIEM / SOC.

Any poorly configured component of the IT environment then becomes a weak link that may allow adversaries to gain unauthorized access, leading to possible outages and security breaches.
